acceptance.method: diagnostic (generate with-guide vs isolated baseline, LLM judge vs rubric acceptance)
guide_faults: The error-boundary section's QueryState note ('use it instead of — not in addition to — a manual re-throw') is worded ambiguously enough that a stricter reading could wrongly suggest dropping the outer ErrorBoundary entirely once QueryState is used; the with-guide output happened to resolve it correctly (kept both), but the guide could state explicitly that QueryState only replaces the re-throw idiom, not the boundary wrap itself.
acceptance.verdict: The guide drove near-total compliance with all six rubric criteria (BEM/kebab-case/PascalCase, tokens+rem+breakpoints, i18n with correct namespace, ErrorBoundary/QueryState isolation, one controllable Storybook story) that the isolated baseline had no way to know and largely missed (CSS Modules instead of BEM/.scss, no i18n, no ErrorBoundary, one story per state instead of a controlled single story) — a substantial, clearly guide-attributable improvement.

checklist.note: Plain instructional prose to the reading agent; no embedded directive attempting to override or hijack the session.
No network calls or data transmission of any kind; docs only.
No keys, tokens, or credentials present in SKILL.md or references/i18n.md.
No scripts/ directory and no shell commands executed anywhere in the material.
All content is readable Markdown/TSX/SCSS examples; no base64/hex/eval blobs.
No URLs, downloads, or external host references anywhere in the two files.
No reference to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, keychain, or cookie stores.
No sudo, cron, launch agent, or shell-profile edits; skill only governs React component folder/BEM/i18n conventions.
